1. (Currently Amended) A method for restoring efficiency of a photovoltaic cell, the method comprising: illuminating a photovoltaic cell such that the photovoltaic cell receives a __time integrated irradiance dose__ equivalent to at least 5 hours of solar illumination; and annealing the photovoltaic cell at a temperature above 90 degrees Celsius for a minimum of 10 minutes, the annealing in response to illuminating the photovoltaic cell.

2. (Currently Amended) The method of Claim 1, wherein the photovoltaic cell comprises a semiconductor wafer, and __wherein the illuminating step comprises__ one of: __illuminating the photovoltaic cell such that the photovoltaic cell receives a time integrated irradiance dose equivalent to at least 20 hours of solar illumination; illuminating the photovoltaic cell such that the photovoltaic cell receives a time integrated irradiance dose equivalent to at least 16 hours of solar illumination while being heated to at least 50 degrees Celsius during the illuminating step; and irradiating the photovoltaic cell in sunlight using a solar concentrator for at least 10 hours, wherein the solar concentrator increases the irradiance of solar illumination on the photovoltaic cell by a factor of 2 to 5__.

3. (Currently Amended) The method of Claim 2, wherein the photovoltaic cell is annealed at a temperature above 130 degrees Celsius, and wherein annealing the photovoltaic cell further comprises illuminating the photovoltaic cell __during the annealing step__.

4. (Currently Amended) The method of Claim 3, wherein illuminating the photovoltaic cell while annealing __the__ photovoltaic cell is performed such that the photovoltaic cell receives a time integrated irradiance __dose__ equivalent to at least 10 minutes of solar illumination.

5. (Currently Amended) The method of Claim 1, wherein __the photovoltaic cell comprises a semiconductor wafer, and__ the semiconductor wafer is a silicon semiconductor wafer.

6. (Original) The method of Claim 1, wherein the photovoltaic cell is annealed at a temperature between 140 degrees Celsius and 210 degrees Celsius for a minimum of 2 hours.

7. (Original) The method of Claim 6, wherein the photovoltaic cell is a thin film photovoltaic cell.

8. (Original) The method of Claim 6, wherein the photovoltaic cell is an amorphous silicon thin film photovoltaic cell.

9. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the photovoltaic cell is illuminated after manufacturing of the photovoltaic cell is complete such that the photovoltaic cell produces electricity when illuminated, __and wherein the illuminating step causes photodegradation of the photovoltaic cell__.

10. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the photovoltaic cell is illuminated with a light source that simulates light from the sun.
